meta.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook, pages last modified 27 Aug 2026; retrieved 14 Sep 2026. Median pay is the US median for the whole occupation in May 2025, not for biosecurity work specifically.
meta.closestNote: Where no handbook occupation matches a role exactly, the nearest one is shown and marked as such.

Epidemiologist.summary: An epidemiologist, also known as a disease detective, investigates the causes of diseases, how diseases spread, and how they can be prevented or controlled.
Epidemiologist.summarySource: CDC NERD Academy, Public Health Careers (updated 22 Aug 2024)

bls.whatTheyDo: Epidemiologists are public health workers who investigate patterns and causes of disease and injury.

Public Health Nurse.summary: A public health nurse plays a vital role in disease prevention and promoting community health and safety, looking at health trends and risk factors, improving access to services, and helping design health education campaigns.
Public Health Nurse.summarySource: CDC NERD Academy, Public Health Careers (updated 22 Aug 2024)

bls.whatTheyDo: Registered nurses deliver and coordinate patient care while educating patients and the public about health conditions.

Biostatistician.summary: A biostatistician looks at data collection methods and analyzes data to help answer health-related questions, using graphs and tables that make the data easier to understand, and explains the limits of the analysis.
Biostatistician.summarySource: CDC NERD Academy, Public Health Careers (updated 22 Aug 2024)

bls.whatTheyDo: Mathematicians and statisticians analyze data and apply computational techniques to solve problems.

Disease Surveillance Officer.summary: Surveillance officers run the systems that watch for disease: collecting reports from clinics and laboratories, checking data quality, and raising the alarm when a signal appears.

bls.whatTheyDo: Epidemiologists are public health workers who investigate patterns and causes of disease and injury.

Physician.summary: Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance.

bls.education: Doctoral or professional degree, plus internship/residency
bls.outlook: 4% growth 2025–35, about as fast as average
bls.whatTheyDo: Physicians and surgeons diagnose and treat injuries or illnesses and address health maintenance.

Nurse Practitioner.summary: Nurse practitioners coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare.

bls.occupation: Nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives, and nurse practitioners
bls.whatTheyDo: Nurse practitioners coordinate patient care and may provide primary and specialty healthcare.

Emergency Medicine Technician.summary: EMTs and paramedics assess injuries and illnesses, provide emergency medical care, and may transport patients to medical facilities.

bls.whatTheyDo: EMTs and paramedics assess injuries and illnesses, provide emergency medical care, and may transport patients to medical facilities.

Respiratory Therapist.summary: Respiratory therapists care for patients who have trouble breathing.

bls.whatTheyDo: Respiratory therapists care for patients who have trouble breathing.

Medical Surge Planner.summary: Surge planners work out how a hospital or health system expands capacity in a crisis: beds, staff, supplies, oxygen, and the agreements with neighboring facilities that make it possible.

bls.education: Bachelor's degree, plus less than 5 years of experience
bls.whatTheyDo: Medical and health services managers plan, direct, and coordinate the business activities of healthcare providers.

Virologist.summary: Virologists study viruses: how they infect cells, evolve and spread, and how vaccines and antivirals can stop them.

bls.whatTheyDo: Microbiologists study microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, algae, and fungi.

Immunologist.summary: Immunologists study how the immune system responds to infection and vaccination, and use that knowledge to design better vaccines and treatments.

bls.whatTheyDo: Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health.

Vaccinologist.summary: Vaccinologists design, test, and evaluate vaccines, from choosing what part of a pathogen to target through clinical trials and post-approval monitoring.

bls.whatTheyDo: Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health.

Bioinformatician.summary: Bioinformaticians write and run the software that turns raw genetic sequence data into meaning: identifying pathogens, tracking variants, and comparing genomes.

bls.whatTheyDo: Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health.

Vaccine Research Scientist.summary: Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health.

bls.whatTheyDo: Medical scientists conduct research aimed at improving overall human health.

Data Scientist.summary: Data scientists use analytical methods and technological tools to uncover patterns and insights in data.

bls.whatTheyDo: Data scientists use analytical methods and technological tools to uncover patterns and insights in data.

Health Informatics Specialist.summary: Health informatics specialists design and manage the information systems that health services and public-health agencies run on, and make their data usable.

bls.occupation: Health information technologists and medical registrars
bls.whatTheyDo: Health information technologists advise organizations on computerized healthcare systems and analyze clinical data.

AI Researcher for Outbreak Detection.summary: AI researchers in this field build and evaluate models that spot outbreaks early in noisy data, forecast their course, or screen for misuse of biological tools.

bls.whatTheyDo: Computer and information research scientists design innovative uses for new and existing technology.

Biosurveillance Analyst.summary: Biosurveillance analysts monitor streams of data from clinics, laboratories, wastewater, animal health, and open sources to detect and characterise biological threats.

bls.whatTheyDo: Epidemiologists are public health workers who investigate patterns and causes of disease and injury.

Biosecurity Specialist.summary: Biosecurity specialists protect laboratories and institutions against the theft, misuse, or accidental release of dangerous biological materials, through risk assessment, access control, training, and policy.

bls.occupation: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians
bls.education: Varies: bachelor's degree for specialists, less for technicians
bls.whatTheyDo: Occupational health and safety specialists and technicians collect data on, analyze, and design improvements to work environments and procedures.

Public Health Policy Analyst.summary: Policy analysts research how laws, budgets, and programs affect health security and write the briefings and options that decision-makers act on. Employers include government, legislatures, think tanks, and non-profits.

bls.whatTheyDo: Political scientists study the origin, development, and operation of political systems.

Emergency Management Director.summary: Emergency management directors prepare plans and procedures for responding to natural disasters or other emergencies and help lead the response.

bls.education: Bachelor's degree, plus 5 years or more of experience
bls.outlook: 4% growth 2025–35, about as fast as average
bls.whatTheyDo: Emergency management directors prepare plans and procedures for responding to natural disasters or other emergencies and help lead the response.

Medical Anthropologist.summary: Medical anthropologists study how culture, belief, and social structure shape health, illness, and the way communities respond to outbreaks and interventions.

bls.whatTheyDo: Anthropologists and archeologists study the origin, development, and behavior of humans.

Behavioral Health Scientist.summary: A behavioral scientist studies why people behave the way they do and what factors influence their decisions and behaviors.
Behavioral Health Scientist.summarySource: CDC NERD Academy, Public Health Careers (updated 22 Aug 2024)

bls.education: Varies by specialty; usually a doctoral degree, plus internship/residency
bls.whatTheyDo: Psychologists study cognitive, emotional, and social processes and behavior.

Disaster Mental Health Counselor.summary: Disaster mental health counselors support survivors, families, and responders during and after emergencies, often through the Red Cross, health systems, or humanitarian agencies.

bls.occupation: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors
bls.whatTheyDo: Mental health counselors advise people on a range of issues, such as those relating to addictions or depression.

Veterinary Epidemiologist.summary: Veterinary epidemiologists investigate disease in animal populations and the risk it poses to people, working across farms, wildlife, and food systems.

bls.whatTheyDo: Veterinarians care for the health of animals and work to protect public health.

Wildlife Disease Ecologist.summary: Wildlife disease ecologists study how pathogens circulate in wild animals and what makes them spill over into livestock or humans.

bls.outlook: 4% growth 2025–35, about as fast as average
bls.whatTheyDo: Zoologists and wildlife biologists study animals and how they interact with their ecosystems.

Climate Change and Health Researcher.summary: These researchers study how a changing climate shifts the geography and timing of infectious disease, and what health systems should do about it.

bls.whatTheyDo: Environmental scientists and specialists conduct research or investigations to protect the environment or human health.

Strategic National Stockpile Manager.summary: Stockpile managers decide what medical countermeasures a country holds in reserve, keep them in date and ready, and get them to the right place within hours of a request.

bls.whatTheyDo: Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization's supply chain.

Cold Chain Specialist.summary: Cold chain specialists keep vaccines and other temperature-sensitive products within range from manufacture to the point of use, including in places with unreliable power.

bls.whatTheyDo: Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization's supply chain.

Humanitarian Logistics Coordinator.summary: Humanitarian logistics coordinators move supplies, equipment, and people into emergencies, managing warehouses, transport, and customs across borders.

bls.whatTheyDo: Logisticians analyze and coordinate an organization's supply chain.

Science Journalist.summary: Science journalists report on outbreaks and biosecurity for the public, explaining the evidence and holding institutions to account.

bls.whatTheyDo: News analysts, reporters, and journalists keep the public updated about current events and noteworthy information.

Risk Communication Expert.summary: A health communication specialist creates communication strategies, messages, and products that translate technical information into culturally relevant, timely, and actionable guidance for the public.
Risk Communication Expert.summarySource: CDC NERD Academy, Public Health Careers (updated 22 Aug 2024)

bls.whatTheyDo: Public relations specialists create and maintain a positive public image for the organizations they represent.

Pandemic Preparedness Trainer.summary: Preparedness trainers design and deliver courses, drills, and exercises so that responders and institutions have rehearsed before a real event.

bls.education: Bachelor's degree, plus less than 5 years of experience
bls.whatTheyDo: Training and development specialists plan and administer programs that train people and improve their skills and knowledge.

PPE Designer.summary: PPE designers develop protective equipment, such as masks, respirators, gowns, and gloves, that protects wearers better and can be worn for long shifts.
